newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes steady in thin late-day trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes steady in thin late-day trade.

text.p: U.S. cash crude oil prices were steady in thin activity late on Monday, traders said.
Some traders extended the Easter holiday to await the reopening of London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on Tuesday.
May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $20.35-45 a barrel, down 30 cents from late Thursday's cash market.
The generally weak expiry of April products contracts on NYMEX pulled the outright price downward, traders said.
The May/June WTI spread was flat.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked at WTI/Cushing minus 33-29 cents a barrel.
WTI/Midland was at WTI/Cushing minus 32-30 cents, with 31 cents last changing hands.
Heavy Louisana Sweet/Empire was last heard done at minus 65 cents after trading at minus 80 cents earlier. The range was pegged at minus 75-70 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded at minus $2.38.
Eugene Island traded at minus $2.37, moving nearly in tandem with WTS in a continued weak pattern fomented by plentiful supplies.
Analysts say the upcoming gasoline season should begin to mop up some of the market's excess supplies in the next few months.
